content.value_statement: Adding libraries can create version sprawl and unreviewed dependencies. This skill guides approval, version lookup, catalog updates, and build verification.
actual_capabilities: Requires approval before adding a third-party dependency.
Directs agents to research the latest stable library version.
Shows how to add versions and libraries to gradle/libs.versions.toml.
Recommends running a Gradle build or sync task after changes.
Warns against hardcoding versions in build.gradle.kts files.
limitations: It does not choose dependencies without user input.
It does not validate license, vulnerability, or maintenance status by itself.
It assumes the project uses a Gradle version catalog.
It does not provide exact dependency coordinates for every library.

use_cases.title: Add an Android library
use_cases.description: An Android developer can add a requested library through the version catalog after approval.

use_cases.title: Review dependency need
use_cases.description: A maintainer can require alternatives and justification before new third-party code enters the project.

use_cases.title: Verify dependency changes
use_cases.description: An AI coding agent can update catalog entries and run the relevant build task for validation.

prompt_templates.title: Add One Dependency
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single approved library.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add the requested Android library. Explain why it is needed, ask for approval, then update the version catalog.

prompt_templates.title: Check Necessity First
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review before adding new third-party code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether this dependency is necessary. Compare it with existing project options, then ask me before making any file changes.

prompt_templates.title: Update Catalog And Verify
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the latest stable version, add the dependency through the Gradle version catalog, update the needed module, and run a relevant build task.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Dependency Choice
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced comparison of a proposed dependency against alternatives.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this proposed dependency against manual implementation and existing libraries. Recommend whether to add it, then prepare the catalog update if approved.

output_examples.input: Add Retrofit to the Android app after approval.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains the need, checks the latest stable release, updates the version catalog after approval, and reports the build result.

output_examples.input: Decide whether a new image library is worth adding.
output_examples.output: The assistant compares existing options with the requested library, summarizes tradeoffs, and asks for approval before editing files.

output_examples.input: Move a requested dependency into the version catalog.
output_examples.output: The assistant adds catalog entries, avoids hardcoded module versions, and verifies the project with a relevant Gradle task.

best_practices: Ask for approval before editing dependency files.
Use the latest stable release from a reliable source.
Run a relevant Gradle task after changing the catalog.
anti_patterns: Adding a dependency before explaining why it is needed.
Hardcoding library versions in module build files.
Skipping build verification after dependency changes.

faq.question: Does this skill install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. It instructs the agent to ask for approval before adding a new third-party dependency.

faq.question: Which project file does it target?
faq.answer: It targets the Gradle version catalog at gradle/libs.versions.toml.

faq.question: Does it require web access?
faq.answer: It recommends a web search to find the latest stable library version.

faq.question: Can it update build.gradle.kts directly?
faq.answer: It discourages hardcoded versions in build.gradle.kts and prefers catalog references.

faq.question: How does it verify the change?
faq.answer: It recommends running a Gradle build or sync command after the catalog update.

faq.question: Is it limited to AnySoftKeyboard?
faq.answer: The workflow comes from AnySoftKeyboard, but it fits Gradle projects that use version catalogs.
